transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... I just haven't been myself lately. 

Ever since a good friend of mine from choir passed away so suddenly, I've just been having a really hard time handling things. I find myself crying over silly things, like the church potluck lists, and I get all worked up about phone calls that I used to handle easy. I've even started missing our church planning meetings, and... well, I never would have missed those before. I just don't feel right.
When you are alone, do you find yourself having unwanted, vivid memories or nightmares about your friend's passing?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I think about her a lot, of course... but I don't have bad dreams about her passing, or, you know, memories that just pop up out of nowhere and feel really vivid like that. It's more just... feeling really sad and overwhelmed. But no, no nightmares or anything.
Aside from the church meetings, have you noticed that you no longer enjoy or take pleasure in other hobbies or activities you used to find fun?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean... I still like doing my usual things around the house. I still enjoy working in my garden and reading my books. 

It's really just the church activities that I've been backing away from. I think maybe because that's where we spent so much time together, so it's just harder to be there. But as for my other hobbies... no, I still find them enjoyable.
